When the war ended there were millions of displaced persons in Germany: forced labourers,
prisoners of war, refugees. Under the agreement made at Yalta most Soviet citizens were sent home,
many against their will, and many who went back were sent on to camps; others did what they could to stay.
Those who stayed lived for years in DP camps run first by the United Nations relief agency and then by the International
Refugee Organization. Zinaida, widowed at Weener in April 1945, stayed with her children.
She married Wacław Stelmasik, a Polish former prisoner of war who had been a farm labourer at Weener,
and the family lived in the camps at Osterhauderfehn and Westrhauderfehn and then at Varel and Bockhorn,
by the Jade. America took refugees slowly, under the Displaced Persons Act of 1948 and then the Refugee Relief Act
of 1953, and in July 1956 Zinaida and her sons flew from Hamburg to New York.
